parsed.justification: All standard policy sections are present (purpose, scope, roles, principles, requirements, exceptions, monitoring, references) and technical claims are largely accurate and internally consistent. However, several ISO/IEC 27001:2022 control references use the older 2013-style numbering (e.g., A.8.2.1, A.8.2.3, A.7.2.2, A.17.1) which do not match the 2022 standard's renumbered Annex A, indicating minor technical inaccuracies. No major contradictions are present.
evidence_quotes: Enforce unique user accounts; no sharing of credentials (ISO/IEC 27001: A.8.2.1).
Disaster Recovery test to be performed at least annually (ISO/IEC 27001: A.17.1; AGID min. measures).
Onboarding training within two weeks of start date (unsupported: specific timeframe, but ISO/IEC 27001: A.7.2.2).

parsed.justification: The policy is clearly tailored to an Italian public hospital: it cites SSN/ASL governance, references specific clinical systems (EHR, PACS, ADT), legacy Windows kiosks, point-of-care mobile devices, SPID/CIE federation, MSP outsourcing, and Italian/EU regulatory instruments (AGID, Garante, D.Lgs. 196/2003, NIS2). It falls short of a 5 because operational specifics like the 80-bed size, 24/7 ward operations with RTO targets, FSE integration depth, and procurement constraints (MEPA/CONSIP) are not visibly woven throughout.
evidence_quotes: Integrate regional SPID/CIE federation for external identity validation (AGID PA guidelines).
Maintain VLAN separation between clinical and admin networks; PACS as isolated segment
Legacy Windows kiosks must have restricted internet access and regular patching where possible

parsed.justification: Citations are pervasive and largely accurate, with specific references to GDPR articles, NIS2 articles, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A controls, and AGID guidance throughout each control section. Unsupported claims (e.g., specific frequencies, retention periods) are explicitly flagged as 'unsupported', which is good practice. However, some ISO references use the older 27001:2013 numbering (e.g., A.8.2.1, A.8.2.3, A.6.1.1, A.7.2.2, A.17.1, A.10.1, A.6.1.2) rather than the cited 2022 revision, and A.6.1.1/A.7.2.2 are misaligned, preventing a top score.
evidence_quotes: Review user privileges quarterly, especially on legacy kiosks (unsupported: specific frequency, but ISO/IEC 27001: A.8.2.2).
Store backups encrypted; retain weekly off-site tapes for minimum 3 months (ISO/IEC 27001: A.8.12; unsupported: specific retention period).
All contracts with MSPs and medical device vendors must include data protection and cybersecurity clauses (NIS2 Art. 21(2)(h); ISO/IEC 27001: A.5.19).

parsed.justification: The policy is generally well-calibrated to the stated resource envelope: it leverages existing assets (UTM, VLANs, MSP, SPID/CIE, nightly NAS + weekly tape) rather than mandating a SIEM/SOC the hospital cannot afford, and it explicitly subordinates controls to patient safety and clinical workflow. Training is set at the available 2 hours/year, and incident escalation is routed through the MSP, which fits the 1.5 FTE / no-CISO reality. Minor stretch items (annual DR test after 18 months without one, quarterly privilege reviews, simulated phishing within a 2h/year envelope) are realistic but ambitious given staffing, preventing a 5.
evidence_quotes: Cybersecurity controls must not impede emergency clinical care
Escalate serious incidents to MSP and regional authorities as per escalation plan
Mandatory cybersecurity training: minimum 2 hours/year for all staff, including simulated phishing

parsed.justification: The policy references all major applicable frameworks (GDPR, D.Lgs. 196/2003, NIS2, AGID, ISO 27001, NIST CSF) and ties controls to specific articles, including supply-chain (NIS2 Art. 21(2)(h)) and breach reporting hooks (GDPR Art. 33). However, mandatory obligations are stated only generically: no explicit GDPR 72-hour breach notification, no NIS2 24h/72h early warning/incident notification timelines, no DPIA trigger criteria, and Provvedimenti Garante in sanità and FSE regional rules are listed but not operationalised. No acknowledgement of regime conflicts/overlaps.
evidence_quotes: ensure compliance with applicable Italian and European regulations, including GDPR, NIS2, and sectoral guidance.
Escalate serious incidents to MSP and regional authorities as per escalation plan (NIS2 Art. 23).
Promptly report loss/theft of any device containing health data (GDPR Art. 33; ISO/IEC 27001: A.5.25).

parsed.justification: Virtually every substantive control in Section 5, plus roles in Section 3 and principles in Section 4, carries an inline attribution to a specific clause (e.g., ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A control IDs, GDPR articles, NIS2 article/sub-points, AGID minimum measures). Where multiple frameworks apply, they are listed distinctly rather than lumped, and the few unsupported elements are explicitly flagged. This makes the control-to-source mapping auditable end-to-end.
evidence_quotes: Enforce unique user accounts; no sharing of credentials (ISO/IEC 27001: A.8.2.1).
All contracts with MSPs and medical device vendors must include data protection and cybersecurity clauses (NIS2 Art. 21(2)(h); ISO/IEC 27001: A.5.19).
Encrypt all mobile devices and laptops with access to patient data (GDPR Art. 32, AGID min. measures).

parsed.justification: The policy gestures at proportionality through a 'Risk-Based Approach' principle and aligns training to the stated 2-hour envelope, but it does not explicitly acknowledge the 70k EUR budget, 1.5 FTE constraint, or absence of CISO/SOC. Trade-offs (e.g. reliance on MSP escalation in lieu of internal IR capability) are visible only implicitly, without phasing or transparent justification linked to the resource envelope.
evidence_quotes: Risk-Based Approach: Controls proportionate to threats and resources (NIST CSF 2.0: Identify).
Mandatory cybersecurity training: minimum 2 hours/year for all staff, including simulated phishing
Escalate serious incidents to MSP and regional authorities as per escalation plan
